memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Write on them all the words of this law when you have crossed over to enter the land the Lord your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, promised you. And when you have crossed the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I command you today, and coat them with plaster." — Deut 27:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Again the instruction is repeated: write down all the words of the law once you enter the land God promised. God wanted His words permanently recorded, not left to fading memory. And the place chosen was Mount Ebal — which, as we will see, was the mountain of the curse. Right where the weight of God's law would be felt, His words were set in stone.

Notice how often this passage repeats "the land the Lord your God is giving you." It was a gift, promised long ago to their ancestors and now being fulfilled. God keeps His word across generations. What He promised Abraham, He was delivering to Abraham's descendants centuries later.

That same faithfulness holds for us. God is not casual with His promises. What He has said, He does — sometimes long after we expect, but always in His time. The land "flowing with milk and honey" was a specific gift to Israel, so we do not read it as a promise of wealth for ourselves. But the God behind the promise has not changed. He remains a promise-keeping God.

And every promise finds its final "Yes" in Christ (2 Cor 1:20). Whatever God has assured you in His Word, you can build your life on it, because the One who promised is faithful.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I truly trust that God keeps His promises, even when they are slow?
2. How has God shown His faithfulness across the seasons of my life?
3. What promise of God do I need to lean on today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, You keep every word You speak. Thank You for Your unchanging faithfulness. Help me build my life on Your sure promises in Christ. Amen.
